$\Delta T = 43 . 2\text{s}$

questions.q: A person moved from $A$~to $B$ on a circular path as shown in figure. If the distance travelled by him is $60m$, then the magnitude of displacement would be : (Given $\cos 135 ° = - 0 . 7$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The distance travelled by the person& $d$~will be equal to the arch length.

$⇒ d = R\theta$

$⇒ 60 = R \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)

$⇒ R = $\dfrac{60 \times 4}{3\pi} = \dfrac{80}{π}$m$

Now the magnitude of displacement can be found using subtraction of vectors. Therefore,

\left|$s\right| = $\sqrt{{R2}^{2} + {R1}^{2} - 2{R}_{1}{R}_{2}cos\theta}$⇒ \left|$s\right| = $\sqrt{R^{2} + R^{2} - 2R^{2}\cos 135 °}

$⇒ $\sqrt{2R^{2} - 2R^{2}\left(- 0 . 7\right)}

$⇒ $\sqrt{3 . 4R^{2}} = \sqrt{3 . 4\left(\dfrac{80}{π}\right)2}

$⇒ R = 47m$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The angle made by the vector on& $xaxis$~is~

$\theta = 90 ° - 30 ° = 60 °$

Let the vector be~$\overset{→}{a}$.

It is given that

~${a}_{y} = 2\sqrt{3} ⇒ asin60 ° = 2\sqrt{3} ⇒ \dfrac{a\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2\sqrt{3} ⇒ a = 4$

$x$~component is~${a}_{x} = acos60 ° ⇒ {a}_{x} = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 2$

questions.q: Two vectors $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ have equal magnitudes. If magnitude of $\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}$ is equal to two times the magnitude of $\overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B}$, then the angle between $\overset{→}{A}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$& will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& \left|\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}\right| = 2\left|\overset{→}{A} - \overset{→}{B}\right|$~

We have,~

$A^{2} + A^{2} + 2A^{2}cos\theta = 4 \left($A^{2} + A^{2} - 2A^{2}cos$\theta\right)

Simplifying we get~

$2A^{2} + 2A^{2}cos$\theta =$8A^{2} - 8A^{2}cos$\theta

$⇒ 1 + cos$\theta =$4 - 4cos$\theta

$⇒ 5cos$\theta =$3 ⇒ cos$\theta = \dfrac{3}{5}$⇒ \theta = \cos^{- 1}$\dfrac{3}{5}

questions.q: If $Z = \dfrac{A^{2}B^{3}}{C4}$, then the relative error in $Z$& will be&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $Z = \dfrac{A^{2}B^{3}}{C4}$

When~quantities are multiplied or divided, the relative error in the result is the sum of the relative errors in the multipliers.

So,~$\dfrac{∆ Z}{Z} = \left[\dfrac{∆ A}{A} + \dfrac{∆ A}{A} + \dfrac{∆ B}{B} + \dfrac{∆ B}{B} + \dfrac{∆ B}{B} + \dfrac{∆ C}{C} + \dfrac{∆ C}{C} + \dfrac{∆ C}{C} + \dfrac{∆ C}{C}\right]$

Thus, relative error is~

$\dfrac{∆ Z}{Z} = \left[$2 $\times $\dfrac{∆ A}{A} +3 $\times $\dfrac{∆ B}{B} +4 $\times $\dfrac{∆ C}{C}\right]$

$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Rules for significant figures:

1. All non-zero numbers are significant

2. Zeros between two non-zero digits are significant

3. Leading zeros are not significant

4. Trailing zeros to the right of the decimal are significant

5. Trailing zeros in a whole number with the decimal shown are significant

6. Trailing zeros in a whole number with no decimal shown are not significant

From above rule, we get

(A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.q: A body of mass $( 5 \pm 0 . 5 ) kg$ is moving with a velocity~of $( 20 \pm 0 . 4 ) ms^{- 1} .$ Its kinetic energy will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy is given by,

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

Differentiating the above equation,

$dK = \dfrac{1}{2} ( v^{2}dm + 2mvdv )$

Dividing by~$K$,

$⇒ \dfrac{dK}{K} = \dfrac{dm}{m} + \dfrac{2dv}{v}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dK}{1000} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{5} + \dfrac{2 \times 0 . 4}{20}$

$⇒ dK = 100 + 40 = 140$

$⇒ KE = ( 1000 \pm 140 ) J$

questions.q: Two forces $P$ and $Q$, of magnitude $2F$ and $3F$, respectively, are at an angle $\theta$ with each other. If the force $Q$ is doubled, then their resultant also gets doubled. Then, the angle $\theta$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
\left|\overset{→}{P}\right| = 2F, \left|\overset{→}{Q}\right| = 3F$

\left|\overset{→}{R}\right| = \sqrt{P^{2} + Q^{2} + 2PQcos\theta}$

$= \sqrt{4F^{2} + 9F^{2} + 12F^{2}cos\theta} = F\sqrt{13 + 12cos\theta}$

If $Q$ is doubled

$2\left|\overset{→}{R}\right| = \sqrt{4F^{2} + 36F^{2} + 24F^{2}cos\theta} = F\sqrt{40 + 24cos\theta}$

$4\left(13 + 12cos\theta\right) = 40 + 24cos\theta$

$12 = - 24cos\theta$

$cos\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = {120}^{°}$

questions.q: The length of a metallic wire is increased by $20 %$ and its area of cross-section is reduced by $4 % .$ The percentage change in resistance of the metallic wire is~________ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

$l ' = 1 . 2lA ' = 0 . 96A$

Using the formula~$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$,~the new~resistance is~

$R^{'} = \dfrac{1 . 2ρl}{0 . 96A}$

$⇒ R^{'} = 1 . 25R$

$⇒ \Delta R = 1 . 25R - R = 0 . 25R$

Hence, the percentage increase is~

$= \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 25R}{R} \times 100 = 25 %$

GIven vector are& $\overset{→}{A} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)m$ and $\overset{→}{B} = \left(\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)m$

Component of $\overset{→}{A}$ along $\overset{→}{B} = \overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{^}{B}$

$= \overset{→}{A} \cdot \overset{→}{B}\left|\overset{→}{B}\right| = \dfrac{2 + 6 - 2}{{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {2}^{2}}= \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$
